## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyaaniyata* ("2. Sitting alone with a woman", Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Aniyata 2) constitutes the second of the two undetermined (*aniyata*) disciplinary rules within the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates cases where a trustworthy female lay follower observes a Buddhist monk sitting alone in private with a woman; if she charges him with a disciplinary breach that entails either temporary suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) or an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*), and the monk acknowledges the act, he is dealt with according to whichever category of offense he admits having committed. An English translation of the rule and its exposition has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
